tickets.body:
## Context

Plan b.jf1; Idea b.ftd; approved PRD t1.ftd.y5; SRD t1.ftd.hj; Epic t1.jf1.r8. Planning artifacts and PM approval are in tickets/handoff/b.ftd/Plans/b.jf1/e3/planning/. E2 all Tasks are done and its accepted source is b8236bbc; E2 Epic remains active because the user owns its closure. User explicitly authorized scoped E3 hatch/build despite that status and later draft siblings. Preserve E2 bounded answer guards, committed-waiting admission, unknown-origin proof holds, acknowledgement-before-output, finite cancellation and public input safeguards. No E4 resume/load/reuse/life-switch, installation, groups or help work. SendKeys literal text and Enter remain separate operations; no arbitrary concurrent-caller atomicity promise.

## Outcome

Replace busy follow-up refusal with bounded, conversation-bound FIFO after the current turn and outstanding decisions. Preserve complete Unicode/newline text, initial-prompt priority and one active turn. Give controls priority, cancel every affected submission explicitly within existing bounds, protect ordered lifecycle records and prevent transient replay. Keep /clear and /new visibly refused until Task 2.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Complete all reviewed source, behavioral, documentation, advice and quality scope below.
- Final settled make test-sandbox passes; retain failed receipts and actual limitations.
- Do not mark the Task done until its exact-commit required scheduler gate is accepted.

## Execution boundary

User: “make test-sandbox is yours, Docker groups and any TLA+ come to me via a scheduler handoff, TLA+ only if spec/tla changes.”

Execute repository tests, scripts and binaries only through `make sandbox` or `make test-sandbox`, with fresh isolated HOME, AD store, socket and owned processes. Never touch the real `~/.config/agent-director` or `~/.agent-director`. Never access/edit `.claude`, log in/out, or read, copy, hash or change credentials. Existing Cursor login stays as is; separately authorized live work runs isolated under `~/ad-codex/ftd/` and stops if login is unreachable. No host tests/binaries, local Docker TESTPLAN groups/collectors, TLC, parsers, scheduler submissions or pushes. Only actual changed `spec/tla/**` model inputs warrant affected-model scheduler jobs, with reasons; do not manufacture model changes or baseline jobs. AD never derives state, identity, permissions or liveness from screen text. Local commits are coordinator-owned on feature/b.ftd with scope b.jf1. Technical decisions are recorded in the SRD; escalate only genuine product questions.

## Run Integration After This Task

Interface changed: Input admission, queued dispatch, cancellation and transcript correlation across the owned Cursor gateway.

tickets.body:

## Execution boundary

User: “make test-sandbox is yours, Docker groups and any TLA+ come to me via a scheduler handoff, TLA+ only if spec/tla changes.”

Execute repository tests, scripts and binaries only through `make sandbox` or `make test-sandbox`, with fresh isolated HOME, AD store, socket and owned processes. Existing Cursor login stays as is; separately authorized live work runs isolated under `~/ad-codex/ftd/` and stops if login is unreachable. No host tests/binaries, local Docker TESTPLAN groups/collectors, TLC, parsers, scheduler submissions or pushes. Only actual changed `spec/tla/**` model inputs warrant affected-model scheduler jobs, with reasons; do not manufacture model changes or baseline jobs. ## What Needs to Change

- Represent complete submissions in one observable acceptance order with bounded resource use and explicit refusal when capacity or eligibility prevents admission.
- Bind accepted submissions to current launch and confirmed conversation at acceptance; preserve complete text and submission identity independent from later ACP request IDs.
- Run ordinary submissions FIFO, one active prompt, after prior turn and outstanding decision constraints permit progression.
- Reuse reporter.verifyReport, runtime/pane verification and durable request predicates; preserve committed-waiting handoff and saved initial-prompt priority.
- Separate ordinary submissions from permission/plan choices and controls. Keep /clear and /new visibly refused in Task1.
- Preserve public send-keys/read-pane/pause contracts; no new public Cursor control API.

## Key Files

- internal/cursorhost/admission.go
- internal/cursorhost/terminal_linux.go
- internal/cursorhost/terminal_other.go
- internal/cursorhost/session.go
- internal/cursorhost/report.go
- internal/cursorhost/requests.go
- internal/cursorhost/protocol.go
- pkg/api/sendkeys.go — contract dependency
- internal/tmux/calls_socket.go — contract dependency
- internal/store/request_proof.go — durable eligibility dependency

## Acceptance Criteria

- Human typing, bracketed paste and successive multiline API submissions preserve Unicode/newlines as distinct complete prompts without duplication or carried text.
- Follow-ups accepted during a running turn execute FIFO without cancelling that turn.
- No submission starts against an unconfirmed, changed, retired or mismatched launch/conversation; input consumed before startup eligibility cannot become future work after startup.
- Committed-waiting reservation survives the hook tail; saved initial prompt retains priority.
- Still-open permission/plan decisions block dispatch. Turn completion, acknowledgement, native claim or pipe output cannot manufacture proof that unknown-origin requests are gone.
- Saturation explicitly refuses without silently dropping/replacing accepted work or indefinitely blocking work/controls.
- Pending, pane-hash, permission-answer and dialog safeguards remain effective.

tickets.title: Prioritize interruption and shutdown with finite, explicit queue cancellation
tickets.body:
## Context

Current interruption/local exit/eligible pause retain a fixed three-second cancellation deadline. Queuing creates races between input consumption, turn completion, pending output and cancellation; bounded shared input channel and synchronous reports require attention. In-memory request retirement is not durable proof a dialog disappeared.

## Execution boundary

Existing Cursor login stays as is; separately authorized live work runs isolated under `~/ad-codex/ftd/` and stops if login is unreachable. No host tests/binaries, local Docker TESTPLAN groups/collectors, TLC, parsers, scheduler submissions or pushes. Only actual changed `spec/tla/**` model inputs warrant affected-model scheduler jobs, with reasons; do not manufacture model changes or baseline jobs. AD never derives state, identity, permissions or liveness from screen text. Local commits are coordinator-owned on feature/b.ftd with scope b.jf1. Technical decisions are recorded in the SRD; escalate only genuine product questions.


## What Needs to Change

- Give interruption and terminal controls priority over waiting ordinary submissions while retaining observable input order.
- Cancel active work, retire outstanding decision-response authority and visibly identify each affected not-started submission cancellation.
- Prevent input consumed during cancellation from automatically restarting work later.
- Preserve the first cancellation deadline through repeated interruption, policy cancellation and authorization-hold release.
- Integrate queue cancellation with local exit, eligible pause, signals, transport/runtime failure and owned shutdown.
- Prevent accepted outbound prompts from starting after cancellation; treat partial/uncertain output honestly, no retry or false zero-delivery assertion.
- Reuse requestController, guarded serialized writer and owned termination/reporting. Unknown-origin durable holds require existing valid proof or owning-spawn end.

## Key Files

- internal/cursorhost/session.go
- internal/cursorhost/admission.go
- internal/cursorhost/terminal_linux.go
- internal/cursorhost/requests.go
- internal/cursorhost/protocol.go
- internal/cursorhost/report.go
- internal/cursorhost/process_linux.go — lifecycle dependency
- pkg/api/pause.go — public guard dependency
- internal/store/cursor_permission.go — authority dependency

## Acceptance Criteria

- Interrupt cancels active and affected not-started work, preserves conversation identity, never automatically restarts work.
- Controls remain effective under ordinary-input/outbound pressure; cancelled queued prompts never later produce prompt calls.
- Repeated interrupts and hold release cannot extend the existing three-second cancellation deadline.
- Cancellation retires queued allow and deny while preserving ack-before-output, both guards, bounded store acquisition/post-wait checks and no uncertain replay.
- Menu choices cannot answer retired requests; independent question denial retains semantics.
- Exit is never model text; exit/eligible pause visibly cancel queue and report ended only after confirmed owned-runtime termination.
- Kill/crash cannot restore transient work; caller restart or attach/detach alone preserves gateway/conversation.
- Public pause/dialog guards and Claude/Codex behavior remain unchanged.
